channel.title: Israel 2026 Election Polling: latest polls
channel.description: Every major published poll for Israel’s 2026 Knesset election, newest first. Built, analyzed and annotated by Ron Levi, University of Toronto, with Claude Code (Anthropic).

item.title: Flash Analysis: two small parties could decide 8 seats
item.description: A party needs at least 3.25% of the vote to win any seats. There were 34 polls in the last two weeks. 9 of them gave Ofer Winter's party (Amcha Israel) 4 seats. The other 25 gave it no seats, because it came in under 3.25%. Hendel and Zelekha's party (the Reservists) got 4 or 5 seats in 19 of the polls and no seats in the other 15. If either party gets less than 3.25% on election day, its votes are left out when the 120 seats are divided, so each party that does get in wins a slightly larger share. Surplus-vote agreements, which let two parties pool their leftover votes, apply only to parties that pass 3.25%. They cannot be assigned to a party that falls below 3.25%. In any event, neither of these two parties has signed one. Either way the Netanyahu bloc stays between 53 and 55 seats and the Change bloc between 50 and 52, short of 61.
